title: Competing managed claims under mandatory shared-state hydrology

dependency_gate.implementation_rule: No DUMMY-15 model or tests before DUMMY-14 qualification and implementation-baseline rebinding.

documented_points: UserDemand allocation can use demand_priority when allocation is active.
Allocated flows are bounded by demand.
Allocation uses sequential/lexicographic objectives by demand priority.
Allocation results distinguish demand, allocated flow and supplied flow.
The physical layer attempts realization after allocation.
public_authority_binding.non_equivalence: DUMMY-15 will be a one-Basin analytical priority oracle, not a reproduction of the Ribasim JuMP allocation model or its physical supplied-flow implementation.

purpose: Reintroduce the original water-conflict question with two managed claims competing for one surface store while a mandatory state-dependent surface-groundwater transfer is realized.

root_irrigation.recipient: root store inside represented three-store boundary
root_irrigation.accounting: surface loss and root gain; internal transfer

external_demand.accounting: surface loss only; external system sink

physical_exchange.management_status: not a managed claim and not clipped merely to preserve either demand

exact_single_basin_oracle.physical_capacity_step: Use the qualified DUMMY-10/DUMMY-13 shared-state management solve with R_total to obtain the exact realizable total managed withdrawal M=U_root+U_ext and physical exchange V.
exact_single_basin_oracle.priority_step: Allocate the exact realized total M lexicographically: satisfy the higher-priority managed claim up to its request, then allocate any remainder to the lower-priority claim.
exact_single_basin_oracle.invariant: For fixed R_total and physical state, changing only priority order changes the split (U_root,U_ext) but not M, V, h_s1 or h_g1.
exact_single_basin_oracle.combined_ledger: Delta(W_root+S_surface+S_groundwater)=-U_ext when no external root forcing is active.

hypotheses: For the canonical state, total realizable managed withdrawal is 32 m3 regardless of which of the two managed claims has higher priority.
Priority order changes only the split of the fixed realizable total in the one-Basin oracle; it does not change V, surface endpoint or groundwater endpoint.
When root irrigation has priority, the canonical realized split is U_root=32,U_ext=0.
When external demand has priority, the canonical realized split is U_ext=20,U_root=12.

Because root irrigation is internal but external demand leaves the represented system, changing priority changes combined three-store storage loss even though the surface/groundwater physical endpoint is unchanged.
Physical exchange V is never reduced solely to protect either managed claim.
No managed claim may receive more than its request and the sum of realized claims equals the exact coupled managed total M.
Current shortages remain diagnostics; only accepted root storage affects the next root irrigation request.

If total physical managed capacity exceeds the higher-priority request, residual capacity is transferred to the next priority without changing physical exchange beyond the effect of total managed withdrawal.
Reversing the sign of V must not change priority bookkeeping semantics.
If all managed claims are fully realizable, reversing priority changes neither deliveries nor the physical endpoint.
In the preregistered reverse-exchange scarcity case, total managed realization is 48 m3 with V=-28 m3 regardless of priority; only the managed split and resulting root memory/system loss change.

future_forecast_realization_extension.question: After the exact same-state priority oracle qualifies, add a separate forecast-allocation versus actual-realization experiment where predicted availability is larger than physically realizable availability.
future_forecast_realization_extension.reason: Do not mix priority semantics and forecast-error semantics in the first DUMMY-15 qualification.

boundaries: no claim that this is Ribasim's full allocation optimizer
no network routing, route priorities or fairness objective
no forecast/allocation mismatch in first-stage DUMMY-15
no production SWAP irrigation authority claim

reverse_exchange_scarcity.interpretation: Priority bookkeeping is unchanged when physical exchange reverses sign; groundwater drainage can increase the total managed capacity but does not become a managed allocation.
